overview: Moderator Danielle Balocca hosted Garbage to Garden President Tyler Frank and resident Christina Elaine to discuss the success and implementation of Medford’s curbside composting program. The group reviewed participation statistics, the science of industrial-scale composting, and strategies to mitigate common concerns such as rodents and odors.

items.title: Introductions and local favorites
items.summary: Moderator Danielle Balocca introduced guests Christina Elaine and Tyler Frank, who shared their favorite local dining spots as an icebreaker.

items.title: Status of Medford's composting program
items.summary: Tyler Frank reported that 44% of Medford households have enrolled in the composting program, which is currently considered one of the most successful in the state.

items.title: Accepted materials and processing locations
items.summary: Frank explained that because the program uses large-scale industrial composting at Brickens Farm, it can accept meat, dairy, bones, and certified compostable paper products.

items.title: Resident perspective on household impacts
items.summary: Christina Elaine described how composting reduced her household's trash volume and eliminated kitchen odors caused by food waste.

items.title: Community values and circular economy
items.summary: The participants discussed how composting aligns with Medford’s values of stewardship, resource sharing, and building a local circular economy.

items.title: Program enrollment and logistics
items.summary: Residents can sign up at medfordcomposts.com to receive a starter kit, including a bin and compostable liners.

items.title: Mitigating rodent and odor concerns
items.summary: The guests clarified that secure, latching compost bins are more effective at deterring rodents than traditional trash bags and explained that composting involves no more labor than standard waste disposal.

items.title: Closing remarks
items.summary: Tyler Frank advised against using garbage disposals for food waste and encouraged all residents to attempt the program to help maintain Medford's lead in state participation.
